hepatic deiodinases are not essential for maintaining euthyroidism.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the euthyroid status is not dependent on hepatic Dio1, and that the liver is not the primary site of regulation for TH metabolism in mice.
hepatic deiodinases are dispensable for the regulation of circulating TH levels, whereas their expression is important for the regulation of hepatic TH-responsive gene transcription and metabolism.
the liver is not a critical organ in the maintenance of the circulating levels of T(4) and T(3), and that the liver is a target organ for THs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hepatic deiodinases are dispensable for the homeostasis of serum thyroid hormones, but that they are required for the maintenance of a normal hepatic T(3) response.
the thyroid axis is not a "closed system" and that the liver can be bypassed to maintain normal circulating levels of TH.

hepatic Dio activity is not required for the maintenance of the euthyroid status in mice.
